story.title: On Money
story.text: It is the unfortunate reality of the world in 2025 that any project that grows beyond a handful of interested parties needs to address the subject of money. There is a lot packed into this little five letter word, and so it's worth diving in a bit into what we mean when we talk about money.
>_See also [https://money.dreyeck.ch/view/on-money On Money by Ralf B.]_

story.title: On Community-based Currencies
story.text: [[People Powered Money]] follows several currency and currency-like things which I will hereby just call currencies for ease. I define currency in [[What Is Money?]], and the book does not offer a formal definition, which is fine since they have to answer to people who care, and I do not. What is, and is not a currency, isn't all that important anyways, all that's important is we're talking about mediums of exchange: something that one person can give to, or do something with, to receive something of value from a second person.
question

story.title: On Time
story.text: Where to begin? Even that question introduces confusion. "Where" connotes a location, something that Time is included in in our universe, but most of us would hardly consider a point in time to be a "where." "To begin" describes a future point in time that demarcates some separation, after which something will come that hasn't happened before. Is there anything more human than conveying anticipation of some future event?

story.title: Time Is Money
story.text: Most of us have the dubious privilege of being able to trade our labor for money, and should that labor be less taxing than other ways of spending our time, say childcare or chopping wood all day, then we can say there is a correlation between our time, and our money. For those of us working hourly, this correlation is direct. The more we work, the more we get paid. In places with overtime this is often felt 1.5 times as much.

story.title: Temporal Value
story.text: Consider an apple, fallen on the road, not yet found by worm or weather. A merchant on their way to market happens upon it and picks it up, adding it to an already picked bushel in their cart. That apple, not a product of their labor, or perhaps anyone's labor, has the same monetary value as the rest of the apples. Thus we see that while time and money are _correlated_, one does not cause the other.

story.title: What Else Do We Value
story.text: You ready for a reframe? What if Utility and Happiness are really valuing the same thing, which, for lack of a better term, we'll call Eudaimonia. We may ask then what are the differences in what they value? My opinion is that the rubric in which they exist is one of who is involved in the valuing.

story.text: So again, Time is Money established an exchange relationship between these two constructs as measurements of value. To discuss it we first had to establish [[What Is Money]], and imply that we know (we do not) what is Time (a phrase I will leave unlinked for now <-- a concept of [[Temporal Value]]). Love feels like something we need to more confine than define in this context, so let's start there.

story.title: Companionate Love
story.text: Well all those other pages about Love-like things play a part, but this is the real business for what we care about here. Companionate love is the love felt between two individuals who share some sort of relationship. This could be a familial relationship, a friendship, or an amorous one. The neurobiology of the companionate love in these cases is similar, and the neural pathways are actually reused, meaning as biological entities we just love and love and love.

story.title: Conation
story.text: So in Europe this thing called the Enlightenment happened, and from it the cohort of folks in Europe transitioned from totally religious to mostly religious, but with some science. There were some who were more into science than others, and these tried to reconcile the existing theologies with science.

story.title: Conative Value
story.text: Like the other values, [[Monetary Value]], [[Temporal Value]], and TBD Value, Conative Value should have units. Like any good measure, these units should have subdivisions, and while the smallest unit is arbitrary, it should be of comparable size to say a second and a penny. Let us call this unit a point.

story.title: Spending Love Points
story.text: We haven't quite gotten to the currency part of all of this yet, but we're headed towards a practical implementation of all this eventually I hope, so here's what we have to work with: phone, wallet, keys, (maybe) watch, (maybe) accessories. Whatever it is needs to go on one or more of those things and be as easy as taking a piece of paper from your wallet and handing it to someone.

story.title: Agency Is Love Is Time Is Money
story.text: Before this gets out of hand, let me assure you that we're gonna stop at four of these. But since we went down the prairie vole hole for Love, I figured it'd be best to just go all the way, and speak to the last part of this whole business, and that is Agency.

story.title: What Is Agency
story.text: It's been pretty vogue the last 30-50 years in philosophy to contend that Free Will doesn't exist. This is usually followed with some paragraphs about how this shouldn't be discouraging, I guess because they didn't have a choice.

story.title: Human Action
story.text: I saw a headline the other day about how [https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com web3] is selling domains for people to attach all of their things to, wallet, passport, deeds, indulgences, who knows? The notion that crypto bros would be leaning into people putting _more_ onto the blockchain rather than encouraging people to run for the hills made me sad cry.

story.title: Big Reveal
story.text: It's us dummies! We value our agency, not the machine's, and every single thing that is using the machine to take away agency needs to be undone.

story.title: What Does Agency Measure
story.text: To describe an event in our universe requires three things: space, time, and something. Space is decomposed into three orthogonal vector spaces we know as dimensions, and because time is involved in these descriptions we call it a dimension too (I thought there was more to it than that, but then I read Minkowski's paper on it, and I don't think there is really).

story.title: What Does Agency Measure part Two
story.text: I've invoked a dangerous word with "system." It's probably the most dangerous thus far out of everything used, but I mean it in a simple form here as I'm talking about computing systems, and computing systems are, by definition, finite and deterministic. They progress in a step-wise fashion from state to state, driven by a clock, which, while fast, is also finite.

story.title: What Is Privacy
story.text: Privacy is a word that gets bandied about all over the place in my home of these United States, and when we talk about the internet it's really easy to conflate privacy with sharing an email address, so to drive this point home I'm going to talk about the most contentious and heated topic in this country: abortion.

story.title: How Rights Work in the US
story.text: If you went to elementary school in the US, you may know that we hold some truths to be self evident, and that some of those are that man was endowed by his creator with certain inalienable rights. That chief amongst these are Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness.

story.text: Without context, this page is certainly going to get me into some trouble, so let me do a bit of a recap.

story.text: I've spent most of my professional life as a people manager. The people I manage tend to like me as a manager since I spend my time letting them do their jobs, helping them to do them by removing stupid bs around them, and encouraging them to actual avail themselves of the benefits and opportunities the company they work for makes available.

story.title: What Is Work
story.text: In Physics, Work is defined as Force x Distance, which means if you commute to an office, do stuff all day, and commute home, you've done no Work (since total distance is then 0). This means we need a different definition and that physicists may want to rethink their relationship with the real world.

story.title: PTO A Medium Of Exchange Of Love In A Marketplace
story.text: Let's say there are these things called potatoes, which for brevity's sake I shall abbreviate as PTO. We can represent PTO by a combination of a decimal value, and some symbol, let's say 🥔. So I can have 🥔5.75 PTO.

story.title: What Are Potatoes?
story.text: My job gives me 🥔7.25/hr PTO and calls them potatoes. What are potatoes then? Are they a currency? Are they Money? Are they Love?

story.title: US Government Doesn't Tax Transactions Of Love
story.text: Back when the Bush tax cuts went into effect, I did some research on historical tax rates, and was utterly shocked by what I found. If you don't already know, and I asked you what the highest income tax rate was in say 1962 would your first guess be 63%?

story.title: Gacha Game Economics
story.text: The ease of distribution in the app stores gave rise to free-to-play games as a viable monetization strategy. Games that are free have been a hallmark of gaming since the beginning, using them to get people to pay even more money is somewhat new. No genre has mastered the art form quite as well as gacha games, a sub-genre of games which utilize gambling-like rewards to get kids coughing up quarters.

story.title: So Who's Footing The Bill?
story.text: Whales.

story.title: So Why Don't We Do That
story.text: Well kind of the whole problem with relying on whales is that they have extra money to spend because they can afford staples. So the only things they're going to spend money on are things that aren't useful beyond entertainment value. So devs are stuck building things like games instead of more useful things like better grocery delivery systems.

story.title: Game Of Beds
story.text: I moved back to Portland right as Game of Thrones was taking off on HBO. I had sold or donated everything I owned other than three clear totes and a bicycle when I left Chicago so when I arrived I picked up two essential items, a TV and a bed. For the TV I headed to the closest Best Buy, and for the bed I searched for nearby mattress stores.

story.title: Here's Why
story.text: People in general aren't big fans of taxes, and Americans in particular have an aversion given that we kind of fought a revolution over these inescapable impositions. Still, a government's going to need funding, and in the States we have at least three to worry about, local, state, and federal, and so the tax man comes for us all.

story.title: The Earth Is Very Big
story.text: The Sun is even bigger than the Earth. If we go by surface area, it's about 12,000 times bigger or four orders of magnitude. That is, as my toddler would say, "pretty big."

story.title: What Does This Have To Do With Agency?
story.text: In [[What Is Agency]] I wrote, "Your desire to do things is often curbed by your ability to do them." You see, it is not the case that there are no jobs in Vancouver, Washington, but there are no mattress stores there. Jobs are more complex than mattresses, and so mattresses got to the endgame first. Every mattress ends up being sold in Oregon because the choice between buying one there and buying one in Washington is easy.

story.title: How Bad Does Oregon Need To Get Before Someone Opens A Mattress Store In Vancouver?
story.text: Well as much as I'd like to go down the road of answering this question, people get the agita when you start talking about bad things in the real world. So we'll return to the virtual world.

story.title: Sales Tax Be Damned
story.text: I present before you two goods of equal utility, we'll call them widgets. You need a widget. The first widget costs $20 with a 10% sales tax for a total price of $22. The second widget costs $22 and $2 of every purchase is used to plant trees.

story.title: Start Opening Washingtonian Mattress Stores.
story.text: In Economics this is called a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitution_effect Substitution Effect] where an unrelated change in relative price causes consumer behavior to change. It's nothing crazy.

story.title: Bridges To Washington
story.text: Before you can build a bridge to Washington, it has to exist. When the Oregon Territory was established in 1847, it included Washington. If this had been admitted as a state, we'd've gotten our bridges, but there'd be no reason to cross them for mattresses since sales tax would be the same on both sides.

story.title: Tektronix
story.text: In the fall of 2000, an 18 year old planetnineisaspaceship sat down at what should have been his first class at Reed College (he had signed up for the 8a Calc class like a dummy. This class was at 9a), and was greeted by his first streaming video meme:

story.title: MAGICal
story.text: Naming things is hard. In a Wizard of Earthsea by Ursula K. Le Guin constructs a magic system where knowing an entity's true name is the magic. It's a way of holding power over them, so powerful that the humble apprentice protagonist is able to best a dragon merely by guessing its name.

story.title: Where You Draw The Line Is Up To You
story.text: I draw the line at [[Fours]]. The Universe started off as mostly Hydrogen and Helium, collapsed in places into galaxies, which then had parts that collapsed into stars, those stars blew up, collapsed into new stars, formed some planets and moons, and on one of those things critters started showing up and eventually one of them woke up one day and started stacking things.

story.title: How Does Magic Work?
story.text: Ok, so it's like this. Everything is waves man, but they can also be like not waves y'know? Particles maybe. And there're these things called fields, and the waves are part of the fields, but the particles aren't because one is quantized and the other isn't. And there are four things called forces, but one maybe isn't a force because all it does is redefine the curvature of space-time...

story.title: Make It Fun.
story.text: The machines are telling me the opposite of entropy is syntropy, and that syntropy is...

item.title: The Earth Is Very Big
item.text: The Sun is even bigger than the Earth. If we go by surface area, it's about 12,000 times bigger or four orders of magnitude. That is, as my toddler would say, "pretty big."

item.title: What Does This Have To Do With Agency?
item.text: In [[What Is Agency]] I wrote, "Your desire to do things is often curbed by your ability to do them." You see, it is not the case that there are no jobs in Vancouver, Washington, but there are no mattress stores there. Jobs are more complex than mattresses, and so mattresses got to the endgame first. Every mattress ends up being sold in Oregon because the choice between buying one there and buying one in Washington is easy.

item.title: How Bad Does Oregon Need To Get Before Someone Opens A Mattress Store In Vancouver?
item.text: Well as much as I'd like to go down the road of answering this question, people get the agita when you start talking about bad things in the real world. So we'll return to the virtual world.

item.title: Sales Tax Be Damned
item.text: I present before you two goods of equal utility, we'll call them widgets. You need a widget. The first widget costs $20 with a 10% sales tax for a total price of $22. The second widget costs $22 and $2 of every purchase is used to plant trees.

item.title: Start Opening Washingtonian Mattress Stores.
item.text: In Economics this is called a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitution_effect Substitution Effect] where an unrelated change in relative price causes consumer behavior to change. It's nothing crazy.

item.title: Bridges To Washington
item.text: Before you can build a bridge to Washington, it has to exist. When the Oregon Territory was established in 1847, it included Washington. If this had been admitted as a state, we'd've gotten our bridges, but there'd be no reason to cross them for mattresses since sales tax would be the same on both sides.

item.title: MAGICal
item.text: Naming things is hard. In a Wizard of Earthsea by Ursula K. Le Guin constructs a magic system where knowing an entity's true name is the magic. It's a way of holding power over them, so powerful that the humble apprentice protagonist is able to best a dragon merely by guessing its name.

item.title: Where You Draw The Line Is Up To You
item.text: I draw the line at [[Fours]]. The Universe started off as mostly Hydrogen and Helium, collapsed in places into galaxies, which then had parts that collapsed into stars, those stars blew up, collapsed into new stars, formed some planets and moons, and on one of those things critters started showing up and eventually one of them woke up one day and started stacking things.

item.title: How Does Magic Work?
item.text: Ok, so it's like this. Everything is waves man, but they can also be like not waves y'know? Particles maybe. And there're these things called fields, and the waves are part of the fields, but the particles aren't because one is quantized and the other isn't. And there are four things called forces, but one maybe isn't a force because all it does is redefine the curvature of space-time...
